input.content:
Biogas plant BGA7 is a flexibilised energy-crop plant that also digests pig slurry and runs its tanks as a serial cascade. A solid feeder with a 60 cubic metre hopper charges the first digester only; a pre-pit (8×5 m, approx. 60 cubic metres) pumps the pig slurry into F1 as well.

Digesters F1 and F2 are connected in series and structurally identical: 24 m diameter and 6 m wall height each, three paddle agitators (F1) resp. one paddle and one long-axis agitator (F2), double-membrane roof with a gas space (including headspace) of 610 cubic metres each, mesophilic at 40 degrees Celsius (313.15 K), fill level 90 percent. The digestate flows from F1 into F2. At the outlet of F2 a screw press separates the digestate; the solid fraction is sold as bedding and fertiliser, the liquid fraction flows into the gas-tight digestate store G1 (32 m diameter, 6 m wall height, two submersible agitators, unheated at approx. 20 degrees Celsius / 293.15 K, fill level 90 percent, gas space including headspace 1,290 cubic metres). A second, open digestate store G2 (36 m diameter, 6 m wall height, two submersible agitators, unheated at approx. 20 degrees Celsius / 293.15 K, fill level 90 percent) without gas capture serves as a seasonal buffer and is covered by an emission-reducing floating layer; as it carries no gas storage roof, its gas space is just the unfilled headspace of approx. 611 cubic metres.

The biogas from F1, F2 and G1 is fed through a gas collecting pipe to two combined heat and power units: CHP 1 with a rated electrical output of 250 kW runs at base load (electrical 40 percent, thermal 45 percent), CHP 2 with 550 kW runs on demand in flexible operation (electrical 42 percent, thermal 43 percent); installed capacity is 800 kW at an average rated output of about 480 kW. The heat supplies a district heating network and a grain dryer. An emergency flare rated 800 cubic metres per hour and a condensate shaft are present.

Substrate feed: 20 t/d maize silage, 4 t/d sugar-beet silage and 3 t/d grass silage through the solid feeder into F1 plus 15 cubic metres per day of pig slurry from the pre-pit into F1.
